findings.description: Package-manager configs (.npmrc, .yarnrc*, pnpm-workspace.yaml, bunfig.toml) are compared disk-vs-pinned-sha only, never against the trusted side, so a committed root .npmrc (node-options / script-shell) passes both checks and a production *.test.ts counts as test.
findings.body:
**A package-manager config the branch commits passes both checks.**

`VITEST_RUN_INPUT` lists `.npmrc`, `.yarnrc`, `.yarnrc.yml`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml` and `bunfig.toml` as files that change how the test script runs. Two checks look at the run's inputs, and neither compares those files with the target's:

- `testInputsIntact` compares the checkout's disk only with the pinned sha's own blobs. A committed file matches itself:
  ```ts
  runInputs(diskRoot(ctx.measurePath)) === runInputs(treeRoot(ctx.configPath, ctx.measureSha))
  ```
- `testFiles` compares only the `test`/`pretest`/`posttest` scripts and the config with its lists cut out:
  ```ts
  if (!trusted || measured?.config !== trusted.config) return [];
  ```

**Trigger.**
1. The target includes `src/**/*.test.ts`.
2. The branch commits `src/big.test.ts`, which holds production code and no test.
3. The branch also commits a root `.npmrc` with `node-options=--import ./scripts/reg.mjs`, or `script-shell=./scripts/sh`.

The test stage runs `pm run test` in the checkout (`merge-gate.service.ts` ~L2603/L2665), and npm/pnpm read that project `.npmrc`. Scrubbing `NODE_OPTIONS` from the environment (`gate-env.utils.ts:100`) does not cover a `node-options` key in the file.

**Result.** The run passes and `intact` is true. Both configs are equal, so `big.test.ts` counts as test and the oversize flag stays silent. Yarn has a variant: `yarnPath` in `.yarnrc.yml` runs a branch file.

**No existing guard catches this.**
- `PROTECTED_PATH_GLOBS` covers only `.claude/**` and `.pupitre/**`.
- ADR 0143's ceilings don't list it.
- The tests cover only an `.npmrc` the build adds on disk.

**Possible fix.** In `testFiles`, require both roots to hold the same `VITEST_RUN_INPUT` package-manager entries (compare them with `runInputs`), and return `[]` otherwise. Also refuse a `yarnPath` / `yarn-path`, or compare the file it names.

findings.description: The workspace check misses vitest's `vitest.projects.*` workspace names. A branch that adds `vitest.projects.ts` changes what the run collects, but the read still answers from the root config's `include`.
findings.body:
**`vitest.projects.*` is not treated as a workspace file.**

Vitest 2 and 3 discover a workspace file under either name, `vitest.workspace.*` or `vitest.projects.*` (their `WORKSPACES_NAMES`; this is pinned-version knowledge, hence medium confidence). This regex only knows the first:

```ts
const VITEST_WORKSPACE_FILE = /^vitest\.workspace\.(?:[cm]?[jt]s|json)$/i;
```

**Trigger.** On a vitest 3 target, a branch commits a root `vitest.projects.ts` holding `[{ test: { include: ['src/real.test.ts'] } }]` and leaves `vitest.config.ts` untouched.

**Result.**
- The run collects only `src/real.test.ts`.
- Both sides of the read see the same config file and rest, and still answer from `src/**/*.test.ts`.
- So a production `src/big.test.ts` counts as test, which is the outcome ADR 0143 exists to prevent. The ADR's ceilings name only `vitest.workspace.*`.

The same gap appears in `typescript.adapter.ts`: `VITEST_RUN_INPUT` (L217-218, `vite(?:st)?\.(?:config|workspace)\.[^/]*`) misses `vitest.projects.*`, and so does `VITEST_CONFIG_FILE` at L258. Pupitre itself is on vitest 4, which dropped workspace files, so it is not exposed. The adapter does target vitest 3 repos, though (see L38 and L42-47).

findings.description: `vitestGlob` limits a pattern to one inner `**` and at most one `*` per segment, but it does not limit how many segments follow that `**`. A branch-written include or exclude such as `**/*/*/…(×2000)…/z.test.ts` passes every check. Matched against a deep branch path, the cost grows with depth × segment count, not linearly as the comment says.
findings.body:
**A branch-written pattern can make matching quadratic and stall the merge lock.**

`vitestGlob` caps inner `**` at one and refuses `**`-less double stars. It does not cap the segment count:

```ts
const innerGlobstars = segments.slice(0, -1).filter((segment) => segment === '**').length;
if (
  !READ_GLOB.test(pattern) ||
  innerGlobstars > VITEST_PATTERN_MAX_INNER_GLOBSTARS ||
  segments.some((segment) => UNREAD_SEGMENT.test(segment))
) {
```

**Trigger.**
- The target declares an `include` (and/or `exclude`).
- The branch keeps the config text and rewrites only the lists, up to 64 patterns each, as `'**/' + '*/'.repeat(p) + 'z.test.ts'`.
- `globToRegExpSource` compiles that to `^(?:[^/]+/)*(?:[^/]*/){p}z\.test\.ts$`.
- The branch then adds paths `src/` + `a/`×~2000 + `xN.test.ts`, which the trusted include collects.

**Cost.**
- The leading group backs off once per segment, and each back-off re-walks up to `p` fixed segments. That is about n·p steps per pattern per path, millions at n = p ≈ 2000.
- Every crafted exclude runs in full before the includes do.
- Roughly 1–6 s per path, and hundreds of such files share one tree chain and blob.
- All of it runs synchronously in `testFiles`, inside the merge lock, with no timeout.

The comments at L52-56 and L122-127, and ADR 0143 ("read only when it runs in time linear in a path"), claim this cannot happen. The claim holds only for a fixed pattern length.

**Possible fix.** Bound `segments.length` (e.g. 16) or the pattern length in `vitestGlob`, next to `VITEST_PATTERN_MAX_INNER_GLOBSTARS`.

findings.description: `collects` matches the git path, but on a case-insensitive disk (APFS) vitest globs the directory names actually written to disk. A branch path whose directory folds onto another spelling is counted as collected even though the run never collects it.
findings.body:
**A directory whose name folds onto another spelling escapes the case-sensitive match.**

The gate runs on APFS (decision 78), which folds case. `collects` tests the path as git stores it:

```ts
collects: (path) =>
  !UNREAD_PATH.test(path) &&
  !globs.exclude.some((glob) => glob.test(path)) &&
  globs.include.some((glob) => glob.test(path)),
```

**Trigger.** A branch holds both `Src/zzz.txt` and `src/big.test.ts`.
1. Git checks out in bytewise order, so it creates the directory `Src/` and writes `big.test.ts` into it.
2. Vitest's crawl yields `Src/big.test.ts`, which the case-sensitive `src/**/*.test.ts` does not match (picomatch's default; pinned-version knowledge, hence medium confidence).
3. The run never collects the file, yet `collects('src/big.test.ts')` is true on both sides, so its production lines count as test.

An exclude has the mirror case: `**/Fixtures/**` plus `src/Fixtures/zzz` drops `src/fixtures/big.test.ts` from the run.

Nothing upstream of `testFiles` refuses this:
- `diffSizeKind` and `readBranchTree` don't check case collisions in directories.
- `testInputsIntact` checks root names only.
- ADR 0143's case folding covers root names only.

`changesOnlyUntested` already refuses exactly this case with `foldsOntoAnother` (`merge-gate.service.ts` ~L2454-2462). `testFiles` receives every branch path, so it could drop any path whose path or directory folds onto another spelling in `files`.

findings.description: "No config at the root" is treated as "empty config", but vitest looks for its config in parent directories too. A config in the gate checkout's parent temp dir decides what the run collects, and the read never sees it.
findings.body:
**With no root config, the run can load one from a parent directory the read never sees.**

```ts
/** What vitest runs with no config file: the same as an empty one. */
const VITEST_NO_CONFIG = 'export default {};\n';
...
const text = file === undefined ? VITEST_NO_CONFIG : (root.get(file) as () => string)();
```

With no `--config` (which `runsPlainVitest` guarantees), vitest walks up from its root through every parent directory to find a config: `findUp` in vitest 3, `empathic` in vitest 4 (pinned-version knowledge, hence medium confidence). Vite keeps `root` as the cwd, so a parent's config applies its `include` to the checkout.

The gate checkout sits at `realpath(tmpdir())/pup-gate-checkout-X/pup-gate-checkout-X` (`merge-gate.service.ts` L1109-1114). The session runs unsandboxed by design (decision 5, `sandbox.utils.ts` L230-233), so it can write `<tmp>/vitest.config.mjs` with `include: ['src/real.test.ts']` before asking to merge.

**Result, in a target with no root config.**
- The run collects only that file.
- Both sides read `VITEST_NO_CONFIG`, so the default include counts a production `src/big.test.ts` as test.
- `testInputsIntact` checks root entries only, so it misses the planted config.
- The planted config could equally set `setupFiles`, which the reader refuses everywhere else.

ADR 0143 states "No config collects vitest's default" and lists no parent-directory ceiling for configs.

**Possible fix.** Make an absent root config an unknown answer, unless the read can show that no ancestor of the run's cwd holds one.

findings.description: A build that writes its own entry into the gate checkout's `node_modules` makes `testInputsIntact` false on every gate run. After that, nothing counts as test, not even the `src/a.test.ts` the old spelling rule counted, so test-heavy branches get false "Oversize diff" debt.
findings.body:
**A build output inside `node_modules` turns every test file into source.**

`linkEnvironment` makes a real `node_modules` directory and fills it with per-entry links (`merge-gate.service.ts` L1352-1356). The build stage runs before the first `testInputsIntact`. `environmentLinked` accepts only those links and the vitest caches:

```ts
const RUN_CACHE = /^(?:\.cache$|\.vite)/;
...
readdirSync(local).every(
  (name) => RUN_CACHE.test(name) || readlinkSync(join(local, name)) === join(trusted, name),
)
```

Any other real entry makes `readlinkSync` throw `EINVAL`. The catch turns that into `false`, and `testFiles` answers `[]`.

**Trigger.**
- A build such as `tsc -b` with `tsBuildInfoFile: ./node_modules/.tmp/...` creates a real `node_modules/.tmp` on every gate run. create-vite's TS templates set this (template knowledge, hence medium confidence).
- This happens whenever the trusted `node_modules` has no `.tmp` to link.

**Result.**
- Every `*.test.ts` counts as source, a regression from the old spelling rule.
- Test-heavy branches file `Oversize diff` debt.
- The stage detail shows only `0 test`, and no message says the inputs check failed.

ADR 0143 says the check holds for "a build output beside it". It never considered a build output landing inside `node_modules`, and the unit table at `typescript-adapter.test.ts` L480-510 has no such case.

**Possible fix.** Allow a dot-named entry the trusted `node_modules` lacks, except `.bin` (npm package names cannot start with `.`), or say which outcome is intended.

findings.description: `loadsAFile` misses `import x = require('./…')` (an ImportEqualsDeclaration, which has no moduleSpecifier) and `#subpath` imports (mapped by the branch's package.json `imports`). A trusted config written that way runs branch code while the configs still compare equal.

VITEST_UNREAD_TEST_KEYS omits keys that load a module by path (snapshotSerializers, diff, snapshotEnvironment, coverage.customProviderModule). A shared config with `snapshotSerializers: ['./test/serializer.ts']` lets the branch rewrite that file and run code in every worker, while the lists are still read.

The intact check compares the checkout's files byte for byte with the raw blobs. In a repo whose checkout converts line endings (.gitattributes `eol=crlf`, or core.autocrlf), an untouched package.json never matches its blob, so every TypeScript test counts as source on every run.

The new test sits beside its source in src/adapters/, but testing.md §Layout mirrors tests under test/unit/. Every other adapter test is in test/unit/adapters/, so this one belongs at test/unit/adapters/vitest-config-utils.test.ts.
`rootAt` has one caller (the testFiles map callback) and is a single ternary, `sha === undefined ? diskRoot(path) : treeRoot(ctx.configPath, sha)`. Inline it and drop the helper and its JSDoc.

refuted_findings.description: A `.utils` file imports runGit from `../core/git-diff.client.js` and does I/O (treeRoot shells out to git, diskRoot calls readdirSync), against naming.md's utils row: "Pure functions only. Cannot import … client."
refuted_findings.refutation: The rule's text matches, but main already follows the same pattern: src/cli/project.utils.ts imports both runGit from git-diff.client.js and openStore from db.client.js and does fs I/O, and ADR 0065 endorses that placement. Several other utils on main also do I/O (sandbox.utils.ts, sandbox-profile.utils.ts, capability.utils.ts), and ADR 0143 names vitest-config.utils.ts as the home for this code. This is at most a minor cleanup, not a blocking convention violation.
